narrative.overview:
This is a readout, not a presentation. The governing fiction is a measurement device: a panel you walk up to and read, where the number is always larger than the thing labelling it, and nothing on the surface exists that isn't reporting a value. Slides are gauges. The audience is taking a reading, not being told a story.

That fiction resolves a lot of decisions at once. Numbers are set in monospace with tabular figures so digits align in columns and change without reflowing. Surfaces are flat — depth comes from hairline rules and three tonal grounds, never from shadow, because a projector crushes soft shadows into mud. Chrome recedes to near-invisibility so the figure it frames can be read from the back of a room. The palette is mostly absent: one blue, used rarely enough that it still means something when it appears.

The register is brand — design is the deliverable here — but the expression is deliberately instrument-like rather than expressive. Credibility is the aesthetic goal.
keyCharacteristics: Monospace tabular numerals carry every figure; the sans family carries every argument
Zero shadows; three tonal grounds and 1px rules do all the layering
One accent blue, rationed; status colors reserved and never decorative
Type scales to the slide box via container queries, not to the viewport
A single −11° diagonal, used three times and no more
Every surface must survive a bad projector, the back row, and a PDF export

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only non-status accent in the system. If a second accent feels necessary, the slide is carrying two ideas and should be two slides.

rules.name: The Reserved Status Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red mean state and nothing else. A green figure is a zero-cost figure; it is never green because green looks positive.

rules.name: The Bookend Rule
rules.body: Observatory Navy appears on the first and last slide only. It marks the entry and exit of the argument.

rules.name: The Container-Query Rule
rules.body: Every type step scales in cqw against the slide's own inline size, not vw. The slide is the container; the viewport is irrelevant.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any figure a reader might compare against another figure is set in the mono family with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The One Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one small-caps mono label per slide, above the headline. It is a wayfinding device, not section furniture.

rules.name: The Ground Alternation Rule
rules.body: Consecutive slides alternate between Ground and Ground Alt. This is the only sectioning device in the system.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface that needs to feel lifted gets a border or a different ground, never a shadow. If neither reads, the layout is wrong.

rules.name: The Rationed Diagonal Rule
rules.body: Three uses of the −11° skew, total: brandmark, eyebrow rule, list bullet. A fourth use has to displace one of the three.

dos: Do scale type in cqw against the slide container, never vw. The projector's aspect ratio is unknown.
Do set every comparable figure in the mono family with tabular-nums.
Do keep body text at Ink Body or darker. 12.5:1 is not excessive here; the back row is eight metres away.
Do alternate Ground and Ground Alt between consecutive slides for rhythm.
Do give caveats real space in the layout — in caption type at the foot of the slide that makes the claim, never a footnote or appendix-only mention.
Do pair every animation with a prefers-reduced-motion alternative, and gate reveals behind no-preference so content is visible by default.
Do keep the print stylesheet working: one slide per page, chrome suppressed.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. Anywhere. Use a border or a different ground.
Don't use a colored border-left / border-right above 1px as an accent. Use a full 1px border plus a wash fill. The tier lane's 3px top border is the only sanctioned edge-key.
Don't let Signal Blue exceed one role per slide, or introduce a second non-status accent.
Don't use a status color as a series or decorative color.
Don't put Observatory Navy on a middle slide.
Don't use Ink Faint for anything the audience reads; it fails AA at 2.98:1 and is confined to presenter chrome.
Don't set status text in an edge value. Good and Warn have ink variants precisely because #14875A and #B26A00 fail 4.5:1 as small type.
Don't add a fourth use of the −11° skew.

Don't animate layout properties (width, height, padding, margin) as a default. Two exceptions are live and documented: the comparison bar's width and the presenter rail's hover height, both one-shot and trivially small. Anything new uses transform and opacity.
Don't use numbered markers as wayfinding alongside the eyebrow. Numbering a real in-slide sequence is content and is fine; numbering slides or sections as furniture is not.
Don't nest containers. A stat tile inside a callout inside a lane is three frames fighting for the same number.
